decisions.reason: The phrase next mode state domain did not define a time slice of D_n. Explicit guard/reset types and (t,R_mn(t,x)) in D_n now make same-clock outgoing IVP admissibility precise; orientation, priority, finite-event conditions and all mathematical estimates are preserved. This is a nonfatal interface clarification of the intended reset semantics.

The Volterra supplier explicitly requires an interval with at least two elements; the original proof invoked it without excluding a=T. The proof now handles a=T by equality and only invokes Volterra when a<T. On that branch the continuous norm difference obeys the integral inequality with L>=0, so the stated Gronwall supplier applies. This is a nonfatal omitted immediate-equality boundary case; no positive-length argument or bound changes.

The lemma propagates a supplied event-time discrepancy; it does not claim to establish transversality or derive that discrepancy from a guard residual. Its estimate holds under the explicitly stronger generality without a crossing-margin assumption. The title describes its application to transverse-event errors. Integral displacement, coordinate-segment reset estimates, earlier outgoing displacement and common-time Gronwall are valid for either ordering, including Delta=0. No item edit is needed.

The state dimension and scalar signed crossing derivative were both denoted d. Renamed only the latter to kappa throughout, preserving the saltation map and hypotheses. The implicit-function argument uses the identity initial-state derivative and nonzero kappa; the proof now distinguishes the actual event-time shift from its linear part, including its little-o remainder. Advancing the earlier outgoing state gives the same minus f-plus timing correction for either sign of the shift.

The cited reset lemma requires a common convex outgoing tube, whereas this theorem assumes only a common outgoing tube; the original invocation is therefore unsupported. The unchanged recurrence follows directly: integrate the incoming continuation and exact earlier outgoing path to bound their displacements, apply the reset state/time Lipschitz estimates along the supplied coordinate segments, and add the evaluation error. The zero-lag branch uses zero displacement. Added the actual Volterra and integral-norm suppliers without strengthening the Statement.

The rejected title inaccurately named only inconclusive although the procedure also returns domain-failure and budget-exhausted; the title now covers explicit failure. Full review also found step 2.1 invoking the reset lemma without its common-convex-outgoing-tube hypothesis: the provider supplies pathwise outgoing bounds, which suffice but do not meet that lemma interface. Replaced that invocation by direct Volterra displacement, reset Lipschitz and triangle estimates, including zero lag and approximate reset error. Complete root coverage, strict orientation, certified ordering, valid provider calls and finite charged budgets justify the unchanged Statement.

The explicit calculations correctly give roots 1/3 and 2/3 with derivatives -1/3 and +1/3 and only the latter enabled. The final sentence nevertheless overstates what complete isolation alone establishes: absence additionally requires no enabled root. Qualified that sentence and called x=t the incoming-mode continuation, since the hybrid state resets at the enabled event. The Example, roots, orientation convention, and finite-budget qualification are preserved.
